blocks.text: Nitrification and denitrification are two phases of the nitrogen cycle. Nitrification converts ammonium (NH4+) to nitrite (NO2-) and nitrate (NO3-), while denitrification converts nitrate to nitrogen (N2). Both are also used in wastewater treatment to remove nitrogen (Table 12.3).

blocks.caption: Differences between nitrification and denitrification (Table 12.3)
rows: Ammonia / NH4+ is converted into nitrite and nitrate
Nitrite and nitrate are converted back to N2, released into the atmosphere
Nitrifying bacteria, aerobic conditions, pH 6.5 to 8.0, optimum 20 to 30 degrees C
Denitrifying bacteria, anaerobic conditions, pH 7.0 to 9.0, optimum 26 to 38 degrees C
Plants absorb the nitrites and nitrates, as they cannot use atmospheric nitrogen directly
Important in wastewater treatment and useful for aquatic life (NH4+ oxidised with NO2- to N2 gas)
Oxidation: NH4+ to NO2- to NO3-; 2NH4+ + 3O2 gives 2NO2- + 4H+ + 2H2O; 2NO2- + O2 gives 2NO3-
Reduction: NO3- to NO2- to NO to N2O to N2; 2NO3- + 10e- + 12H+ gives N2 + 6H2O
